correctness.rationale: Twist compatibility splits every endomorphism as diag(x,B). Direct substitution reduces the complete Nijenhuis identity to (xI-B)(AB-BA)=0. In the split square class, the 2-by-2 commutator has determinant v^2-u^2, so every solution lies in exactly the commuting component or one of the two rank-one-commutator components, giving the three affine 3-spaces. In the nonsplit square class, the determinant equation delta(p-s)^2=(q-delta*r)^2 has only the zero-commutator solution, so B belongs to the quadratic field centralizer. Rank profiles are derived componentwise and independently replayed over F3, F5, and F7.

value.rationale: The family is not an arbitrary slice: it is the nondegenerate multiplicative part of the paper's explicit three-dimensional example, exactly where the later Nijenhuis theory applies. The calculation reveals a structural arithmetic bifurcation invisible over algebraically closed fields: the split square class has three irreducible affine components and many more operators, while the nonsplit class collapses to the quadratic-field centralizer. Exact rank profiles and finite-field counts make the distinction reusable in deformation and operator-moduli calculations.
